docs.title: Indexcards
docs.text:
Indexcards is a web application for studying with index cards, built with Angular and Spring Boot.

Users organise their cards in projects (e.g. one per subject or exam). Each index card is a question/answer pair that is studied either with spaced repetition, where cards are rated and scheduled for their next review, or in a free practice mode that goes through all cards without affecting the schedule.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Projects with an optional exam date; reviews are compressed so all cards are repeated before the exam.
  • Index cards with Markdown and LaTeX math (rendered with MathJax).
  • Images in cards: paste an image from the clipboard directly into the question or answer.
  • Spaced repetition based on the SM-2 algorithm with the ratings Bad, Ok and Good.
  • Practice mode to go through all cards of a project without changing their schedule.
  • Statistics showing how the cards of a project are currently rated.
  • CSV import and export of index cards.
  • Account management including permanent deletion of the account and all its data.
  • Available in English and German.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: The application uses MySQL 5.7. The entities are in indexcards/src/main/java/com/x7ubi/indexcards/models.

docs.title: user
docs.text: A user account. The username is unique (checked by the application), oidc_subject is the Authentik user UUID (token claim sub, unique); it is null for legacy accounts that have not logged in via Authentik yet. Passwords are stored in Authentik, not in the app. role is USER or ADMIN (stored as text); admins can open the analytics page. created_at is the signup date; it is null for accounts created before migration 4.

docs.title: project
docs.text: A project of a user. The name is unique per user (checked by the application). exam_date is optional and used for spaced repetition.

docs.title: indexcards
docs.text:
An index card of a project.

  • question and answer are stored as longblob (byte[] in the entity) containing UTF-8 text. They are converted to strings in IndexCardMapper.
  • assessment is the latest rating of the card.
  • ease_factor, repetitions, interval_days and due_date hold the spaced repetition state. They are NULL for cards that were never rated; the entity then returns the defaults (ease factor 2.5, 0 repetitions, interval 0, due now).

docs.title: indexcardassessment / indexcards_assessment_history
docs.text: Every rating of a card is saved as an indexcardassessment row with its date. The join table indexcards_assessment_history links the ratings to the card.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
Assessment is an enum with the values UNRATED, BAD, OK and GOOD. It is stored as its ordinal (0–3).

Danger

Never reorder or insert values into the Assessment enum. Since the ordinal is stored, this would change the meaning of all existing ratings. New values may only be appended at the end, and the frontend enum in app.responses.ts must be kept in the same order.

docs.title: Deleting
docs.text: Deletes cascade through the entities: deleting a user deletes their projects, deleting a project deletes its index cards, deleting an index card deletes its rating history. Images are not stored in the database; see Backend for how they are deleted.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
The schema is managed with Flyway. Migrations are in indexcards/src/main/resources/db/migration and run automatically when the backend starts. Hibernate only validates that the schema matches the entities (spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate), so the backend does not start if they differ.

Version File Description 1 V1__baseline.sql Initial schema, as previously generated by Hibernate. 2 V2__drop_legacy_join_tables.sql Moves links from the old join tables user_projects / project_index_cards into the foreign keys and drops the tables. 3 V3__project_archive.sql Adds archived and auto_archived_exam_date to project. 4 V4__user_role_created_at.sql Adds role (default USER) and created_at to user.

Databases that existed before Flyway was introduced are marked as version 1 (spring.flyway.baseline-on-migrate) instead of running the baseline script.

To change the schema:

  1. change the entity,
  2. add a new migration V<next>__<description>.sql with the matching SQL,
  3. never edit a migration that has already been deployed.

Tests use H2 and let Hibernate create the schema, so they do not run the migrations.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
The pipeline is a GitHub Actions workflow defined in .github/workflows/pipeline.yml. It runs on every push to main and on every pull request targeting main.

Job Runs on Pull requests Push to main Depends on Build and Test ubuntu-latest yes yes — Linting ubuntu-latest yes yes — Deployment self-hosted no yes Build and Test Deploy documentation ubuntu-latest no yes —

docs.title: Build and Test
docs.text: Builds the backend with Maven on JDK 21 (mvn -B package) and runs all tests. If there are failures, the pipeline fails and the change should not be merged into main.

docs.title: Linting
docs.text:
Checks the indexcards-ui module on Node.js 22:

  1. npm ci
  2. npm run lint — static code analysis with ESLint,
  3. npm run format:check — formatting with Prettier.

Run npm run format locally to fix formatting errors.

Note

The deployment only waits for Build and Test, not for Linting. A lint error therefore fails the pipeline but does not stop the deployment.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Runs only on pushes to main after Build and Test succeeded. It is executed on a self-hosted runner on the server, which stops the running containers and starts containers with the new version using the docker-compose.yml in the repository root. The secrets DB_PASSWORD, AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY, AUTHENTIK_PG_PASSWORD, AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD, AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and RESEND_API_KEY and the variables AUTHENTIK_URL and INDEXCARDS_URL are passed to Docker Compose as environment variables.

See Deployment for details. The app is available at https://indexcard.7ubi.de.

docs.title: Deploy documentation
docs.text: Runs only on pushes to main. It installs MkDocs and runs mkdocs gh-deploy, which builds the site and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. GitHub Pages serves that branch at https://documentation.indexcards.7ubi.de.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
The repository is separated into three parts:

Directory Part Technology indexcards Backend Spring Boot 4.1, Java 21, MySQL, Flyway indexcards-ui Frontend Angular 22, Angular Material, ngx-translate indexcards-docu Documentation MkDocs with the Material theme

Additionally there are:

  • docker-compose.yml — starts database, backend and frontend for the deployment,
  • .github/workflows/pipeline.yml — the pipeline,
  • scripts/bump-version.sh — sets the version of backend and frontend (see Getting Started).
flowchart LR
    Browser -->|HTTP| Frontend["Frontend<br/>(Angular, served by nginx)"]
    Frontend -->|/api/**| Backend["Backend<br/>(Spring Boot)"]
    Backend --> DB[(MySQL)]
    Backend --> Images[/Image storage/]

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: The backend is a Spring Boot REST API in the package com.x7ubi.indexcards. It validates the Authentik (OIDC) access tokens of the users, stores users, projects and index cards in MySQL and stores uploaded images on disk. See Backend.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text: The frontend is an Angular single page application with standalone components and Angular Material. In production it is served by nginx, which also forwards /api/ requests to the backend. See Frontend.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation is written in Markdown under indexcards-docu/docs and generated into a website by MkDocs. It is published to documentation.indexcards.7ubi.de by the pipeline.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
All endpoints are under /api. Request and response bodies are JSON unless noted otherwise.

Except for /api/auth/** and GET /api/images/{id}, every request needs the header

Authorization: Bearer <token>

with an Authentik access token (see Authentication). Errors are returned as a plain text error code, see Error handling.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Users log in at Authentik (OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE; username/password or Google). Every endpoint except the ones below and GET /api/images/{id} requires Authorization: Bearer <access token>. On the first request with a new token subject the backend creates the user account automatically.

docs.title: Get login configuration
docs.text:
GET /api/auth/config → 200 OK (no token required)

{ "authority": "https://auth.indexcards.7ubi.de/application/o/indexcards/", "clientId": "indexcards" }

docs.title: Get account
docs.text:
GET /api/user → 200 OK

{ "username": "jane", "firstname": "Jane", "surname": "Doe", "admin": false }

admin is true if the user has the ADMIN role; the frontend uses it to show the analytics page.

docs.title: Delete account
docs.text:
DELETE /api/user → 204 No Content

Deletes the logged-in user with all projects, index cards, rating history and images.

{ "username": "jane" }

The username must be typed again as confirmation.

Also deletes the user's Authentik account through the Authentik API.

Errors: 401 username_confirmation_mismatch, 503 authentik_deletion_failed (Authentik could not delete the user; nothing was deleted)

docs.title: Get 2FA devices
docs.text:
GET /api/user/mfa → 200 OK

[
{ "type": "totp", "id": "1", "name": "Authenticator app", "created": "2026-10-19T13:06:37Z", "lastUsed": null },
{ "type": "webauthn", "id": "3", "name": "YubiKey", "created": "2026-10-18T10:00:00Z", "lastUsed": "2026-10-19T09:00:00Z" }
]

The user's confirmed second factors, loaded from Authentik. type is totp (authenticator app), webauthn (passkey or security key), email (email code) or static (recovery codes). Devices are set up in Authentik's setup flows, not through this API.

Errors: 503 authentik_mfa_failed

docs.title: Remove a 2FA device
docs.text:
DELETE /api/user/mfa/{type}/{id} → 204 No Content

Deletes the device in Authentik. Only the user's own devices can be removed.

Errors: 400 mfa_device_not_found, 503 authentik_mfa_failed

docs.title: Get all projects
docs.text: GET /api/project → 200 OK, list of ProjectResponse

docs.title: Get project
docs.text: GET /api/project/{id} → 200 OK, ProjectResponse including all index cards

docs.title: Create project
docs.text:
POST /api/project → 201 Created

{ "name": "Biology", "examDate": "2026-12-01" }

examDate is optional (null). Errors: 400 project_name_exists, 400 project_name_too_long

docs.title: Edit project
docs.text:
PUT /api/project?id={id} → 200 OK

Same body as create. If an exam date is set, due dates of the project's cards are capped (see Spaced Repetition).

docs.title: Delete project
docs.text: DELETE /api/project?id={id} → 204 No Content

docs.title: Get index card
docs.text: GET /api/indexCard?id={id} → 200 OK, IndexCardResponse

docs.title: Create index card
docs.text:
POST /api/indexCard → 201 Created

{ "projectId": 1, "question": "What is $2+2$?", "answer": "**4**" }

docs.title: Edit index card
docs.text:
PUT /api/indexCard?id={id} → 200 OK

Same body as create (projectId is ignored). Rating and schedule are not changed.

docs.title: Delete index card
docs.text:
DELETE /api/indexCard → 204 No Content

{ "indexcardId": 5 }

docs.title: Get cards for spaced repetition
docs.text: GET /api/indexCard/quizIndexCards?id={projectId} → 200 OK, list of up to 15 IndexCardResponse, sorted by due date (most overdue first).

docs.title: Rate a card
docs.text:
POST /api/indexCard/assess → 200 OK

{ "indexCardId": 5, "assessment": "GOOD" }

assessment is one of BAD, OK, GOOD. Saves the rating in the card's history and schedules its next review.

docs.title: Import CSV
docs.text:
POST /api/indexCard/import → 201 Created

{ "projectId": 1, "csv": "\"Question 1\",\"Answer 1\"\n\"Question 2\",\"Answer 2\"" }

See Import & Export for the CSV format.

docs.title: Upload image
docs.text:
POST /api/images (multipart/form-data, field file) → 201 Created

{ "imageId": "3f2b8c1e-8f5d-4c7a-9b0e-2a6d1f4e7c90" }

The file must have an image/* content type and be at most 5 MB. Errors: 400 invalid_image

docs.title: Get image
docs.text:
GET /api/images/{imageId} → 200 OK, image/jpeg. No authentication required.

Errors: 400 image_not_found

docs.title: Admin
docs.text: Endpoints under /api/admin/** require the ADMIN role. Other users get 403 forbidden.

docs.title: Get analytics
docs.text:
GET /api/admin/analytics → 200 OK

{
"totals": { "users": 2, "activeProjects": 1, "archivedProjects": 0, "indexCards": 1, "assessments": 1 },
"assessmentDistribution": { "unrated": 0, "bad": 0, "ok": 0, "good": 1 },
"dailyActivity": [ { "date": "2026-09-29", "assessments": 1, "activeUsers": 1 } ],
"dailySignups": [ { "date": "2026-09-29", "count": 2 } ],
"users": [
{
"username": "bob",
"createdAt": "2026-09-29T09:39:25",
"projects": 1,
"indexCards": 1,
"assessments": 1,
"lastActivity": "2026-09-29T09:39:26",
"admin": false
}
]
}
  • assessmentDistribution counts index cards by their current rating.
  • dailyActivity and dailySignups always contain the last 30 days (oldest first, today last); days without activity have 0. activeUsers is the number of distinct users who rated at least one card that day.
  • users is sorted by lastActivity (the latest rating), most recent first; users without ratings come last with lastActivity: null. createdAt is null for accounts created before signup dates were recorded. admin is true for users with the ADMIN role.

docs.title: Make a user admin
docs.text:
PUT /api/admin/users/{username}/admin → 204 No Content

Gives the user the ADMIN role. Doing this for a user who is already an admin changes nothing. There is no endpoint to remove the role.

Errors: 400 username_not_found

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Status Code Meaning 400 project_not_found The project does not exist. 400 indexcard_not_found The index card does not exist. 400 username_not_found The user of the token does not exist anymore. 401 user_not_project_owner The project or card belongs to another user. 401 — Missing, invalid or expired token. 403 forbidden The endpoint requires the ADMIN role.

docs.title: ProjectResponse
docs.text:
{
"id": 1,
"name": "Biology",
"examDate": "2026-12-01",
"indexCardResponses": [ /* IndexCardResponse */ ]
}

docs.title: IndexCardResponse
docs.text:
{
"indexCardId": 5,
"question": "What is $2+2$?",
"answer": "**4**",
"assessment": "UNRATED",
"dueDate": "2026-09-28T10:15:30"
}

assessment is one of UNRATED, BAD, OK, GOOD.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: The backend is a Spring Boot 4.1 application (Java 21) in indexcards/. The package root is com.x7ubi.indexcards.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package Content controller REST controllers, one per resource (/api/auth, /api/project, /api/indexCard, ...). service Business logic, grouped by domain (authentication, project, indexcard, image, user). models JPA entities (User, Project, IndexCard, IndexCardAssessment) and the Assessment enum. repository Spring Data JPA repositories. request Request DTOs, grouped by domain. response Response DTOs, grouped by domain. mapper MapStruct mappers between entities and DTOs (ProjectMapper, IndexCardMapper). jwt The 401 entry point for requests without a valid token (AuthEntryPointJwt). config Spring Security (OAuth2 resource server, AuthentikJwtAuthenticationConverter), CORS and web configuration. exceptions Custom exceptions and the GlobalExceptionHandler. error ErrorMessage — the error codes returned to the frontend.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant F as Spring Security
    participant Ctrl as Controller
    participant S as Service
    participant R as Repository
    C->>F: request with "Authorization: Bearer <access token>"
    F->>F: validate token (Authentik JWKS), map to SecurityUser, set SecurityContext
    F->>Ctrl: authenticated request
    Ctrl->>Ctrl: username = securityUser.getUsername()
    Ctrl->>S: operation(username, request)
    S->>R: load user + entity, check ownership
    S->>R: save / delete
    S-->>Ctrl: response DTO (via mapper)
    Ctrl-->>C: JSON

docs.title: Controllers
docs.text: Controllers are thin. They take the authenticated user as @AuthenticationPrincipal SecurityUser and pass its username to a service. They never return entities, only response DTOs.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Services are split one per operation, not one per entity. For example, index cards have CreateIndexCardService, EditIndexCardService, DeleteIndexCardService, IndexCardAssessmentService, IndexCardQuizService and the read-only IndexCardService.

All index card services extend AbstractIndexCardService, all project services extend AbstractProjectService. These hold the shared repositories and guard methods such as getUser(username), getProjectNotFoundError(id), getIndexCardNotFoundError(id) and getProjectOwnerError(user, project).

When adding a new operation, add a new service extending the matching abstract service instead of growing an existing one.

docs.title: Ownership checks
docs.text:
Nearly every operation follows the same pattern:

  1. load the User by username,
  2. load the target project or index card (throw EntityNotFoundException if it does not exist),
  3. check that the project belongs to the user (throw UnauthorizedException otherwise),
  4. perform the change.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Exceptions are translated into HTTP responses by GlobalExceptionHandler. The response body is a plain error code from ErrorMessage, which the frontend translates (backend.<code> in the i18n files).

Exception Status Example codes EntityNotFoundException 400 project_not_found, indexcard_not_found, image_not_found, username_not_found EntityCreationException 400 project_name_exists, project_name_too_long, invalid_image UsernameExistsException 400 username_exists UnauthorizedException 401 user_not_project_owner, username_confirmation_mismatch AuthentikDeletionException 503 authentik_deletion_failed any other exception 500 Internal server error

When adding a new error, add the code to ErrorMessage and a translation under backend in indexcards-ui/src/assets/i18n/*.json.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is delegated to Authentik (OIDC). The backend is an OAuth2 resource server:

  • Every request's bearer access token is validated against Authentik's signing keys (JWKS), issuer and audience (spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.*, see config/AuthentikJwtAuthenticationConverter.java).
  • The token's sub is mapped to the local user (oidc_subject), which is created on first use (OidcUserProvisioningService). An account is only created for a fresh token (issued at most 5 minutes ago, otherwise 401): an access token stays valid up to 24 hours, so an old token must not re-create an account that was deleted in the meantime.
  • Members of the Authentik group indexcards-admins (token claim groups) get the ADMIN role (AdminGroupService).
  • Passwords are stored and hashed only in Authentik; the backend never sees them.
  • SecurityConfig permits /api/auth/**, /api/test/** and GET /api/images/** without authentication; everything else requires a valid token. Unauthenticated requests get a 401 from AuthEntryPointJwt.

docs.title: Index card content
docs.text: Question and answer are stored as byte[] (@Lob, longblob in MySQL) in the IndexCard entity and converted to and from UTF-8 strings in IndexCardMapper. There is no length limit. The content is Markdown with LaTeX; the backend does not interpret it, except when deleting a user (see below).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
ImageStorageService stores uploaded images as <uuid>.jpg in the directory configured by app.images.storage-path. Only files with an image/* content type are accepted, and uploads are limited to 5 MB.

Images are not linked to users or cards in the database. Cards reference them in their Markdown as /api/images/<uuid>. When a user deletes their account, DeleteUserService scans the user's cards for these references and deletes the image files after the database transaction was committed, skipping images that are still referenced by cards of other users. It also deletes the Authentik user through AuthentikUserDeletionService (Authentik API, service-account token AUTHENTIK_API_TOKEN); if that fails, the deletion is rolled back.

docs.title: Spaced repetition
docs.text: Scheduling is implemented in SpacedRepetitionScheduler. See Spaced Repetition.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Tests are in indexcards/src/test, grouped like the services (admin, image, indexcard, project, user). They use JUnit 5 with an in-memory H2 database configured in TestConfig.java and the *TestConfig.java classes of each feature.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text: The frontend in indexcards-ui/ is an Angular 22 single page application using standalone components (no NgModules) and Angular Material.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
src/
├── app/
│   ├── component/   reusable components (header, card flip, card overview, charts, dialogs, ...)
│   ├── directives/  mathjax and paste-image directives
│   ├── pages/       routed pages (auth, project, indexcard, account, privacy)
│   ├── pipes/       markdownMath pipe
│   ├── service/     http, login, local storage, image and snackbar services
│   ├── util/        helpers (e.g. ISO date conversion)
│   ├── app.routes.ts
│   └── app.responses.ts
└── assets/i18n/     translations (en.json, de.json)

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Path Page Login required /login Login no /login/callback Login callback from Authentik no /signup Redirects to /login no /privacy Privacy policy no / All projects yes /account/delete Delete account yes /project/create Create project yes /project/:id Project with its index cards yes /project/:id/edit Edit project yes /project/:id/createIndexCard Create index card yes /project/:id/editIndexCard/:indexCardId Edit index card yes /project/:id/quiz Spaced repetition yes /project/:id/quiz/stat Statistics yes /project/:id/practice Practice yes ** Page not found no

Protected routes use the LoginRequired guard (service/login/login-required.ts), which redirects to /login if there is no token.

docs.title: Backend communication
docs.text:
All backend calls go through HttpService (service/http/http.service.ts). It wraps HttpClient's get, post, put and delete and

  • adds the Authorization: Bearer <token> header from LoginService,
  • shows errors with SnackbarService, translating the backend error code (backend.<code>),
  • logs the user out on any 401 response, except user_not_project_owner.

New API calls should use HttpService instead of injecting HttpClient directly, to keep this behaviour consistent.

The token is stored in local storage via LocalService and managed by LoginService.

Response types are declared in app.responses.ts. Keep them in sync with the backend's response classes; the Assessment enum must have the same order as in the backend.

docs.title: Rendering cards
docs.text:
Card content is Markdown with LaTeX math:

  1. The markdownMath pipe replaces math regions ($...$, $$...$$, \(...\), \[...\]) with placeholders, renders the Markdown with marked and puts the math back in.
  2. The appMathjax directive typesets the math with MathJax 3, which is loaded from a CDN in index.html. It observes the element and re-typesets when the content changes (e.g. in the editor preview).

MathJax is configured in index.html with the ui/safe extension, which filters potentially dangerous TeX commands from user content.

docs.title: Image upload
docs.text: The appPasteImage directive can be added to a textarea bound to a form control. On paste it compresses the image in the browser (compressImage in image.service.ts: max. 1600 px, JPEG quality 0.82), uploads it to POST /api/images and inserts ![image](/api/images/<id>) at the cursor.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: Texts are translated with ngx-translate. The files are src/assets/i18n/en.json and src/assets/i18n/de.json; add every new key to both. The language is detected from the browser on the first visit and stored in local storage under language.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• ESLint (npm run lint) enforces the app prefix for component selectors (kebab-case) and directives (camelCase).
  • Prettier (npm run format:check) with a print width of 100 and single quotes.
  • Components use ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager and trigger change detection explicitly with ChangeDetectorRef.

Lint and format are checked in the pipeline.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page describes how to run Indexcards locally for development.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Tool Version Used for Java (JDK) 11 Backend Maven 3.6+ Backend build (or use ./mvnw) Node.js 22+ Frontend MySQL 5.7 Database (e.g. via Docker) Python 3.9+ Documentation (optional)

docs.title: Login for local development
docs.text:
The app has no own login anymore; it needs Authentik:

  1. Create a Google OAuth client (see Deployment → Login) with the redirect URI http://localhost:9000/source/oauth/callback/google/.

  2. Create .env in the repository root (not committed):

    AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY=<openssl rand -base64 60 | tr -d '\n'>
AUTHENTIK_PG_PASSWORD=<random>
AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD=<admin password>
AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL=<your email>
AUTHENTIK_URL=http://localhost:9000
INDEXCARDS_URL=http://localhost:4200
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=<client id>
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=<client secret>

  3. docker network create nginx_backend (once), then docker compose up -d mysqldb authentik-db authentik-server authentik-worker.

  4. Start the backend (./mvnw spring-boot:run; its defaults point to http://localhost:9000) and the frontend (npm start), open http://localhost:4200, click Sign in or create account and use Sign up (or Google).

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The backend expects a MySQL database indexcardsdb on port 3306 (host from MYSQL_HOST, default localhost) with user root and password 12345678. The quickest way is a Docker container:

docker run -d --name indexcards-db -p 3306:3306 \
-e MYSQL_DATABASE=indexcardsdb -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=12345678 \
mysql:5.7

The schema is created automatically by Flyway on the first start of the backend.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
cd indexcards
./mvnw spring-boot:run

The backend starts on http://localhost:8080. It validates the access tokens issued by Authentik, so Authentik has to be running (see Login for local development). Uploaded images are stored in ./data/images (see configuration).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The tests use JUnit 5 and an in-memory H2 database, so no MySQL is needed:

./mvnw clean package                                     # build and run all tests
./mvnw test -Dtest=CreateIndexCardServiceTest            # single test class
./mvnw test -Dtest=CreateIndexCardServiceTest#methodName # single test method

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
cd indexcards-ui
npm install
npm start

The app is available on http://localhost:4200. The dev server proxies all requests to /api/** to the backend on http://localhost:8080 (see src/proxy.conf.json).

Command Description npm start Dev server with live reload npm run build Production build into dist/ npm test Unit tests (Vitest) npm run lint ESLint npm run format:check Check formatting with Prettier npm run format Fix formatting with Prettier

Lint and format are checked in the pipeline, so run them before pushing.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
cd indexcards-docu
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The documentation is then available on http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Full stack with Docker
docs.text: The docker-compose.yml in the repository root starts MySQL, backend and frontend together. It is meant for the deployment and requires an external Docker network; for development running the parts separately as described above is simpler.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Backend and frontend share one version number. To change it, run

scripts/bump-version.sh 2.3.0

This updates the version in indexcards/pom.xml, the jar name in indexcards/Dockerfile and indexcards-ui/package.json.

docs.title: Spaced Repetition
docs.text: Scheduling is implemented in SpacedRepetitionScheduler in the backend. It is inspired by the SM-2 algorithm, adapted to the app's three ratings Bad, Ok and Good instead of SM-2's quality score from 0 to 5.

docs.title: State of a card
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning easeFactor 2.5 How fast the interval grows. Never lower than 1.3. repetitions 0 Number of successful reviews in a row. intervalDays 0 Days between the last review and the next one. dueDate now When the card should be reviewed next.

New cards have all these fields set to NULL in the database and use the defaults, so they are due immediately.

docs.title: Rating a card
docs.text:
When a card is rated via POST /api/indexCard/assess, IndexCardAssessmentService stores the rating in the card's history and calls SpacedRepetitionScheduler.schedule:

Rating Repetitions Ease factor Interval Bad reset to 0 − 0.2 (min. 1.3) 1 day Ok + 1 − 0.05 (min. 1.3) 1st: 1 day, 2nd: 3 days, then round(previous × EF × 0.8) Good + 1 + 0.1 1st: 1 day, 2nd: 6 days, then round(previous × EF)

The interval is always at least 1 day. The new due date is now + interval.

Ok grows the interval more slowly than Good (dampening factor 0.8) and slightly lowers the ease factor, so cards that are only known "okay" come back more often.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A new card rated Good every time (ease factor after each rating in brackets):

Review Ease factor Interval 1 2.6 1 day 2 2.7 6 days 3 2.8 17 days 4 2.9 49 days

docs.title: Exam date
docs.text:
If the card's project has an exam date in the future, the interval is capped:

maxInterval = max(1, daysUntilExam / 2)
interval    = min(interval, maxInterval)

This makes sure every card is reviewed several times before the exam, with the reviews getting closer together as the exam approaches. Exam dates today or in the past are ignored.

When a project's exam date is changed (PUT /api/project), applyExamDateCap pulls the due date of every card forward to now + maxInterval if it currently lies later. Ease factor, repetitions and interval are not changed, so the next real rating continues from the card's previous progress.

docs.title: Selecting cards
docs.text:
IndexCardQuizService sorts all cards of a project by due date (ties by id) and returns the first 15. This means overdue cards come first, most overdue first. If fewer than 15 cards are due, the round is filled up with the cards that are due next, so a round is never empty as long as the project has cards.

Practice mode does not use this endpoint; it loads all cards of the project and does not send ratings to the backend.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The application is deployed with Docker Compose using docker-compose.yml in the repository root. The pipeline does this automatically on every push to main.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
Service Container Image / Build Port (host:container) Description mysqldb dbcontainer mysql:5.7 3306:3306 Database indexcardsdb backend backendcontainer indexcards/Dockerfile 8081:8080 Spring Boot backend frontend frontendcontainer indexcards-ui/Dockerfile 4200:80 Angular app served by nginx authentik-db authentikdbcontainer postgres:16-alpine — Database of Authentik authentik-server authentikservercontainer ghcr.io/goauthentik/server:2025.10 9000:9000 Login service (OIDC, Google login) authentik-worker authentikworkercontainer ghcr.io/goauthentik/server:2025.10 — Background tasks, applies blueprints 
flowchart LR
    Proxy[Reverse proxy] --> Frontend["frontendcontainer<br/>nginx :80"]
    Frontend -->|/api/| Backend["backendcontainer<br/>:8080"]
    Backend --> DB[("dbcontainer<br/>MySQL :3306")]
    Backend --> Vol[/"volume image-storage"/]
    DB --> DBVol[/"volume my-db"/]
    Proxy --> Authentik["authentikservercontainer<br/>:9000"]
    Backend -->|JWKS| Authentik
    Authentik --> AuthDB[("authentikdbcontainer<br/>PostgreSQL")]
  • The frontend image builds the Angular app with Node and serves it with nginx (indexcards-ui/nginx.conf). nginx serves the app for all paths (falling back to index.html for client-side routing) and forwards /api/ to backendcontainer:8080.
  • The backend image builds the jar with Maven and runs it on Java 21.
  • The frontend and backend are also attached to the external network nginx_backend, which is used by the reverse proxy on the server. It has to exist before starting: docker network create nginx_backend.

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
Volume Mounted at Content my-db /var/lib/mysql MySQL data image-storage /app/data/images Uploaded images of index cards authentik-db /var/lib/postgresql/data Authentik users, sessions, events

All volumes must be included in backups.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: All containers use the json-file log driver with at most 3 files of 10 MB each, so logs (including nginx access logs with IP addresses) are rotated automatically.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The backend is configured in indexcards/src/main/resources/application.properties. Values can be overridden with environment variables.

Environment variable Default Description DB_PASSWORD — Used by Docker Compose as MySQL root password and for the backend. SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL jdbc:mysql://${MYSQL_HOST:localhost}:3306/indexcardsdb Database URL. SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME root Database user. SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD 12345678 Database password. MYSQL_HOST localhost Database host (if SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL is not set). IMAGES_STORAGE_PATH ./data/images Directory for uploaded images. AUTHENTIK_URL — Public URL of Authentik, e.g. https://auth.indexcards.7ubi.de (no trailing slash). INDEXCARDS_URL — Public URL of the app, e.g. https://indexcards.7ubi.de; used for the OIDC redirect URI. AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY — Authentik's secret key (openssl rand -base64 60 \| tr -d '\n'). Never change it after the first start. AUTHENTIK_PG_PASSWORD — Password of Authentik's PostgreSQL database. AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD — Password of the Authentik admin akadmin, only used on the first start. AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL — Email of akadmin, only used on the first start. AUTHENTIK_API_TOKEN — Secret token of the Authentik service account indexcards-backend (openssl rand -hex 32). Read by the blueprint and sent by the backend to delete Authentik users. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID — OAuth client of the Google Cloud project. GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET — Secret of that OAuth client. RESEND_API_KEY — Resend API key, used by Authentik as SMTP password (smtp.resend.com) to send mail from noreply@7ubi.de. AUTHENTIK_ISSUER http://localhost:9000/application/o/indexcards/ Backend: expected token issuer (set by Docker Compose from AUTHENTIK_URL). AUTHENTIK_JWKS_URI http://localhost:9000/application/o/indexcards/jwks/ Backend: where the token signing keys are fetched. AUTHENTIK_CLIENT_ID indexcards Backend: OIDC client id / expected token audience. AUTHENTIK_API_URL http://localhost:9000/api/v3 Backend: Authentik API used to delete users (set by Docker Compose to the internal Authentik address).

Other settings in application.properties:

Property Value Description spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size 5MB Maximum size of an uploaded image.

docs.title: Login (Authentik)
docs.text:
Users log in through Authentik, either with a username and password stored in Authentik (self-service signup on the login page) or with their Google account. The two kinds of account are not linked. The app never sees passwords or email addresses; the backend only validates Authentik's access tokens.

Every account needs an email address. Signup asks for one (unique, case-insensitive) and creates the account inactive; it is activated when the user opens the confirmation link Authentik sends to that address (valid for 24 hours). Accounts created before email was required are asked for an address on their next login and have to confirm it before they are logged in. Authentik sends the mails through Resend (RESEND_API_KEY); the domain 7ubi.de must be verified in Resend. Google accounts take their address from Google and are not checked for uniqueness.

Two-factor authentication is optional. Users add an authenticator app (TOTP), a passkey/security key (WebAuthn), email codes or recovery codes (static tokens: 10 one-time codes, offered once another factor exists) on the account page, which opens the setup flows indexcards-mfa-totp-setup, indexcards-mfa-webauthn-setup, indexcards-mfa-email-setup and indexcards-mfa-static-setup through the login flow (skipped while the Authentik session is active) and returns to /account. The login flow, and the default source authentication flow for Google logins, then ask for the second factor; users without one log in with their password only. The account page lists and removes devices through the backend, which uses the Authentik API with the service account indexcards-backend. If a user has lost their second factors and recovery codes, delete the device in the Authentik admin (Directory → Users → user → MFA Authenticators).

There is no self-service password reset yet. If a user forgets their password, open Directory → Users in the Authentik admin, select the user and use Create recovery link, then send them the link. Disabling or deleting a user there blocks their login. Sessions that are already open stay valid until their access token expires (up to 24 hours). Authentik is configured by the blueprint authentik/blueprints/indexcards.yaml, which the worker applies on every start.

When a user deletes their account in the app, the backend also deletes the Authentik user through the Authentik API. For this the blueprint creates the service account indexcards-backend with a role that may only view and delete users; its token is AUTHENTIK_API_TOKEN. Authentik superusers are never deleted this way. The OIDC provider uses sub_mode: user_uuid, so the token's sub is the Authentik user UUID, which the backend uses to find the user to delete. If Authentik cannot be reached or refuses, the deletion fails with 503 and nothing is deleted.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. Google OAuth client: In the Google Cloud Console (APIs & Services → Credentials) create an OAuth client ID of type Web application with the authorized redirect URI <AUTHENTIK_URL>/source/oauth/callback/google/. Configure the consent screen with the scopes openid, email and profile, and publish it.
  2. Reverse proxy: Route AUTHENTIK_URL (e.g. auth.indexcards.7ubi.de) to authentikservercontainer:9000 on the nginx_backend network. Pass the Host header and X-Forwarded-Proto: https through, because Authentik builds the token issuer from them and it must equal <AUTHENTIK_URL>/application/o/indexcards/.
  3. GitHub: Create the repository secrets AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY, AUTHENTIK_PG_PASSWORD, AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD, AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL, AUTHENTIK_API_TOKEN, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY and the repository variables AUTHENTIK_URL, INDEXCARDS_URL. Remove the old JWT_SECRET secret.
  4. After the first deployment, log in to <AUTHENTIK_URL>/if/admin/ as akadmin and check under Customization → Blueprints that indexcards was applied successfully. Under System → Settings, check that Event retention is days=365 (stated in the privacy policy).

docs.title: Accounts from the password login
docs.text: The former username/password accounts were not migrated. Migration V6 renamed them to legacy-<username> and removed their password hashes; they cannot log in anymore. Their data stays in the database until it is deleted by hand. Deleting the Authentik user (Directory → Users) does not delete the app account; users do that themselves on the account page, which also deletes their Authentik user.

docs.title: Deploying manually
docs.text:
export DB_PASSWORD=<database password>
export AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY=<base64 key>
export AUTHENTIK_PG_PASSWORD=<database password of Authentik>
export AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD=<password of akadmin>
export AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL=<email of akadmin>
export AUTHENTIK_API_TOKEN=<random token, openssl rand -hex 32>
export RESEND_API_KEY=<Resend API key>
export AUTHENTIK_URL=https://auth.indexcards.7ubi.de
export INDEXCARDS_URL=https://indexcards.7ubi.de
export GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=<client id>
export GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=<client secret>
docker-compose down
docker-compose up --build -d

Database migrations run automatically when the backend starts (see Migrations).

docs.title: Creating an admin
docs.text:
Admins can open the analytics page. Members of the Authentik group indexcards-admins (created by the blueprint) become admins in the app:

  1. The user logs in to the app once.
  2. In the Authentik admin (<AUTHENTIK_URL>/if/admin/), open Directory → Groups → indexcards-admins and add the user.
  3. The user logs out of the app and logs in again. Group memberships are only sent in new access tokens, so an existing session (up to 24 h) keeps the old state.

The group only grants the app's admin role; it gives no rights in Authentik itself. Usernames are not used for this, because users choose them freely. After that, admins can make other users admins from the analytics page; those users don't have to be group members.

Revoking takes two steps. Remove the user from the group (otherwise their next request makes them admin again), then set the role back in the database:

docker exec -it dbcontainer mysql -uroot -p indexcardsdb \
-e "update user set role = 'USER' where username = '<username>';"

The role is read from the database on every request, so this applies immediately.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is hosted on GitHub Pages. The pipeline runs mkdocs gh-deploy, which pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch. docs/CNAME keeps the custom domain documentation.indexcards.7ubi.de on every deploy. To deploy by hand:

cd indexcards-docu
mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Account
docs.text: All projects and index cards belong to a user account, so you need to sign up and log in before using the app.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
Click Sign in or create account on /login. You are redirected to the app's login service (Authentik), where you can log in with your username and password, create a new account via Sign up (username, name, email address and password; the account becomes usable once you open the confirmation link sent to your email address), or log in with Google (on the first Google login you choose a username once). Your Index Cards account is created automatically on the first login, using your name as first and last name (the last word is the surname). Password accounts and Google accounts are separate accounts.

Accounts created before an email address was required are asked for one on the next login and have to confirm it before they can continue. If you forget your password, contact the operator; there is no reset by email yet. The app stores the access token for the current browser tab only; when it expires (after 24 hours) or the backend rejects it, you are logged out and redirected to the login page.

Pages other than login and the privacy policy can only be opened while logged in.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
Under Two-factor authentication on the account page you can add a second factor that the login asks for after your password: an authenticator app (e.g. Aegis, Google Authenticator), a passkey or security key, or a code sent to your email address. Setting one up opens the login service, which brings you back to the account page afterwards. You can add several second factors and remove them there at any time.

Once a second factor is set up, you can also Create recovery codes: ten one-time codes that the login accepts instead of your other factors, e.g. if you lose your phone. Each code works once. The codes are shown only while they are created, so save them somewhere safe (a password manager or a printout). There is one set of recovery codes at a time; to get new codes, remove the recovery codes on the account page and create them again. If you lose access to all second factors including the recovery codes, contact the operator.

docs.title: Logout
docs.text: Open the account menu (the account icon in the top right corner) and choose Logout. This removes the token from the browser. Logging out also ends your session at the login service, so the next login asks for your credentials again.

docs.title: Account page
docs.text: Open the account menu and choose Account (/account). The page shows your first and last name (read-only) and lets you change your username or delete your account.

docs.title: Change username
docs.text: Enter the new username, then click Change username. The new username must not be empty, must be at most 100 characters long and must not be taken by another user. Your login at Authentik is not affected, so you keep logging in with the same credentials.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Show "due today" reminder controls whether the dialog listing the index cards due today appears when you open your projects. It is enabled by default. You can also turn it off directly in the dialog with Don't show this again. The setting is stored in the browser's local storage, so it applies to this browser only and is kept after logging out.

docs.title: Delete account
docs.text:
Deleting your account is done at the bottom of the account page. To confirm, you have to type your username.

Warning

Deleting your account is permanent and cannot be undone.

The following data is deleted:

  • your user account (username, first and last name),
  • all of your projects,
  • all index cards in these projects,
  • your learning progress (ratings, rating history and review dates),
  • uploaded images that are embedded in your index cards (unless another user's card references the same image),
  • your login account (username and password, or the link to your Google account).

If the login service is unavailable at that moment, nothing is deleted and you can try again later.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: The app is available in English and German. On the first visit the language is chosen based on the browser language (German if the browser is set to German, English otherwise) and remembered in local storage.

docs.title: Privacy policy
docs.text: The privacy policy is available at /privacy and linked from the footer and the login page.

docs.title: Admin Analytics
docs.text:
Admins see an app-wide overview of how Indexcards is used. Open the account menu (the account icon in the top right corner) and choose Analytics (/admin). The entry is only shown to admins; other users who open /admin are sent back to their projects. See Creating an admin for how to grant the role.

The page shows:

  • Totals: number of users, active projects (with the number of archived projects below), index cards and ratings.
  • Current rating of all index cards: how many cards are currently unrated, bad, ok and good.
  • Ratings per day and Active users per day for the last 30 days. A user counts as active on a day when they rated at least one card. Hover over a bar to see the date and value.
  • Sign-ups per day for the last 30 days. Accounts created before signup dates were recorded have no date and are not included.
  • Users: one row per user with signup date, number of projects, index cards and ratings, and the time of their latest rating. Click a column header to sort. Admins are marked with an Admin label; every other user has a Make admin button.

docs.title: Making other users admins
docs.text:
Click Make admin in a user's row and confirm the dialog. The user gets the admin role immediately and can open the analytics page, see all users and make further admins. There is no way to remove the role in the app; see Creating an admin for how to revoke it in the database.

Days are based on the server's time zone.

docs.title: Import & Export
docs.text: Index cards can be imported from and exported to CSV files on the project page. This makes it easy to move cards between projects or to create many cards at once in a spreadsheet.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Each line is one index card with two columns: question, then answer. There is no header line.

"What is the capital of France?","Paris"
"What does $E = mc^2$ describe?","Mass-energy equivalence"
Plain question without quotes,Plain answer
  • Values may be wrapped in double quotes. This is required if a value contains a comma.
  • A double quote inside a quoted value is written as two double quotes ("").
  • Leading and trailing whitespace of each value is removed.
  • Lines with fewer than two columns are skipped.
  • Line breaks inside a value are not supported; every line is a separate card.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: Click the import button on the project page and choose a CSV file. All cards from the file are added to the project as new, unrated cards. Existing cards are not changed or replaced, so importing the same file twice creates duplicates.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Click the export button to download all cards of the project as <project name>.csv. Every value is quoted, so the file can be imported again without changes.

The export only contains question and answer; ratings and review dates are not exported. Images are exported as their Markdown link (![image](/api/images/<id>)) and keep working as long as the image exists on the server.

docs.title: Index Cards
docs.text: An index card has a question (front) and an answer (back). Both are required. When studying, the card is shown with the question side up and flipped by clicking or tapping on it.

docs.title: Create and edit
docs.text:
On the project page click Create index card. The editor has an Edit and a Preview tab, so you can check how Markdown, math and images are rendered before saving. Existing cards are edited the same way from the project page.

Editing a card only changes its text; its rating and review schedule stay the same.

docs.title: Markdown
docs.text:
Question and answer are rendered as Markdown. Single line breaks are kept, so you do not need two spaces at the end of a line.

**Photosynthesis** converts:

- light energy
- water and CO₂

into *glucose* and oxygen.

docs.title: Math
docs.text:
LaTeX math is rendered with MathJax. The following delimiters are supported:

Type Syntax Inline $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ or \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\) Display/block $$\int_0^1 x\,dx$$ or \[\int_0^1 x\,dx\]

Math is protected from Markdown, so characters like _ and * inside a formula are not treated as emphasis.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
To add an image, copy it to the clipboard and paste it into the question or answer field. The image is

  1. resized in the browser to at most 1600 px on its longest side and converted to JPEG,
  2. uploaded to the server (max. 5 MB),
  3. inserted into the text as Markdown: ![image](/api/images/<id>).

While the upload is running a placeholder is shown. If the upload fails the placeholder is removed again.

Note

Images are stored under a random id and can be viewed by anyone who knows their link. Do not upload images with sensitive content.

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: Cards can be deleted from the project page. This also deletes the card's rating history.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: A project groups index cards that belong together, for example all cards for one subject or one exam.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After logging in, the start page lists all of your projects together with the number of cards they contain. Click on a project to open it.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
Click the button to create a new project and enter:

Field Required Notes Name yes At most 100 characters. Must be unique among your projects. Exam date no Used by spaced repetition to schedule all reviews before the exam.

docs.title: Project page
docs.text:
The project page shows the exam date (if set) and all index cards of the project, each with its current rating and the date of its next review. From here you can:

  • create a new index card,
  • edit or delete existing index cards,
  • start spaced repetition or practice,
  • open the statistics,
  • import or export cards as CSV.

docs.title: Edit a project
docs.text:
Name and exam date can be changed on the project's edit page. The same rules as for creating apply.

When the exam date is set or moved closer, cards whose next review would fall too late are pulled forward so they are still reviewed in time (see Exam date). The rest of a card's learning progress is not changed.

docs.title: Archive a project
docs.text:
Projects you are no longer studying for can be archived with the archive button on the project page or on the project's card on the start page. You have to confirm archiving in a dialog. The same button restores an archived project. Archived projects:

  • are listed in the collapsible Archived section below your other projects on the start page,
  • are not included in the cards due today,
  • are read-only: their cards can still be studied with spaced repetition or practice and exported, but not created, edited, deleted or imported. The project itself (name, exam date) can still be edited.

A project is also archived automatically on the day after its exam date. This happens only once per exam date: if you restore a project whose exam is over, it stays restored. If you later set a new exam date, the project is archived again once that date has passed.

docs.title: Delete a project
docs.text: Deleting a project also deletes all of its index cards and their rating history. You have to confirm the deletion in a dialog.

docs.title: Studying
docs.text: There are two ways to study the cards of a project: spaced repetition and practice. Both need at least one index card in the project.

docs.title: Spaced repetition
docs.text:
Spaced repetition shows you the cards that are due for review. A round contains up to 15 cards: the cards that are most overdue come first. If fewer than 15 cards are due, the round is filled up with the cards whose review comes up next.

For each card:

  1. read the question and try to remember the answer,
  2. flip the card to check the answer,
  3. rate how well you knew it: Bad, Ok or Good.

The rating is saved immediately and decides when you see the card again:

Rating Effect Bad The card starts over and is due again tomorrow. Ok The card is due in 1 day, then 3 days, then the interval grows moderately. Good The card is due in 1 day, then 6 days, then the interval grows faster over time.

The better you know a card, the longer the gaps between its reviews get. The details of the algorithm are described in Spaced Repetition.

After the last card you are taken to the statistics.

docs.title: Exam date
docs.text: If the project has an exam date, no review is scheduled further away than half the remaining time until the exam. For example, with the exam in 10 days a card is due again in at most 5 days. This makes sure every card is repeated a few times before the exam. Once the exam date has passed it is ignored.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Practice goes through all cards of the project, independent of when they are due. You rate the cards like in spaced repetition, but the ratings are not saved and do not change the review schedule. This is useful for a final run through all cards, e.g. right before an exam.

At the end a chart shows how many cards you rated Bad, Ok and Good in this run. You can practice again or switch to spaced repetition.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text: The statistics page shows a chart of how the cards of a project are currently rated (Unrated, Bad, Ok, Good), based on the latest spaced repetition rating of each card. New cards are Unrated.
